source.public_versification_note: Public 6:1–15 binds Hebrew 5:27–41; public 6:16–81 binds Hebrew 6:1–66. Public 12:4 combines Hebrew 12:4–5, and public 12:5–40 binds Hebrew 12:6–41. Other selected verses bind matching labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Distinguish birth order, transferred rights, and genealogical reckoning without forcing the last clause’s subject.
verses.before: Now the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel—for he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, so that he is not recorded in the genealogy according to the firstborn.
verses.after: These are the descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn. He was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. The genealogy was not to be reckoned by birthright.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel—for he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, so that he is not recorded in the genealogy according to the firstborn.

verses.rationale: Keep political leadership distinct from Joseph’s birthright.
verses.before: Though Judah prevailed over his brothers, and from him came a ruler, the birthright belonged to Joseph.
verses.after: Judah became strong among his brothers, and a ruler came from him, but the birthright belonged to Joseph.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though Judah prevailed over his brothers, and from him came a ruler, the birthright belonged to Joseph.

verses.after: Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, had these sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

verses.rationale: Retain both royal designations and the narrator’s divine agency claim.
verses.before: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria and the spirit of Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, and he took them into exile, namely, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan to this day.
verses.after: So the God of Israel stirred the spirit of Pul king of Assyria and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria. He deported the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria and the spirit of Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, and he took them into exile, namely, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan to this day.

verses.after: Their relatives, heads of ancestral households, numbered 1,760, capable men for the work of serving in God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their kin, heads of their ancestral houses, numbered one thousand seven hundred and sixty—mighty men of strength for the work of the service of the house of God.

verses.rationale: Identify the Merarite branch and every ancestor.
verses.before: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, from the descendants of Merari;
verses.after: From the Levites came Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, a descendant of Merari;
verses.tsw_comparator: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, from the descendants of Merari;

verses.rationale: Keep Mattaniah’s ancestry distinct from the preceding three names.
verses.before: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zikri, son of Asaph;
verses.after: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;
verses.tsw_comparator: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zikri, son of Asaph;

verses.rationale: Retain both pedigrees and the specified residence.
verses.before: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the settlements of the Netophathites.
verses.after: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the Netophathite villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the settlements of the Netophathites.

verses.rationale: Name the four gatekeepers and identify the chief.
verses.before: The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their kin. Shallum was their chief.
verses.after: The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was the head.
verses.tsw_comparator: The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their kin. Shallum was their chief.

verses.rationale: Preserve the east-gate location and continuing service.
verses.before: Until now they have been at the king’s gate on the east. They were the gatekeepers for the camps of the descendants of Levi.
verses.after: They still served at the King’s Gate on the east, the gatekeepers for the Levites’ camps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Until now they have been at the king’s gate on the east. They were the gatekeepers for the camps of the descendants of Levi.

verses.rationale: Keep both present duty and ancestral precedent.
verses.before: Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his kin from his ancestral house—the Korahites—were responsible for the work of the service, guarding the thresholds of the tent. Their ancestors had been over the camp of the LORD, guarding the entrance.
verses.after: Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his fellow Korahites from his ancestral household were responsible for guarding the tent’s thresholds. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the LORD’s camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his kin from his ancestral house—the Korahites—were responsible for the work of the service, guarding the thresholds of the tent. Their ancestors had been over the camp of the LORD, guarding the entrance.

verses.rationale: Retain the narrator’s brief affirmation without expanding it.
verses.before: Phinehas son of Eleazar had formerly been their leader; the LORD was with him.
verses.after: Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their leader in earlier times. The LORD was with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Phinehas son of Eleazar had formerly been their leader; the LORD was with him.

verses.rationale: Keep the particular entrance and named guardian.
verses.before: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.after: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah guarded the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Retain number, local registers, and both appointing figures.
verses.before: All those selected as gatekeepers at the thresholds numbered two hundred and twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in their settlements. David and Samuel the seer established them in their office of trust.
verses.after: In all, two hundred twelve were chosen to guard the thresholds. They were registered by genealogy in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to these positions of trust.
verses.tsw_comparator: All those selected as gatekeepers at the thresholds numbered two hundred and twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in their settlements. David and Samuel the seer established them in their office of trust.

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s tent-and-house language rather than silently replacing it with temple.
verses.before: They and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the house of the LORD—the house of the tent.
verses.after: They and their sons took turns guarding the gates of the LORD’s house, the tent sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: They and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the house of the LORD—the house of the tent.

verses.rationale: Preserve each direction in its original order.
verses.before: The gatekeepers were stationed at the four directions: east, west, north, and south.
verses.after: The gatekeepers served on all four sides: east, west, north, and south.
verses.tsw_comparator: The gatekeepers were stationed at the four directions: east, west, north, and south.

verses.rationale: Keep the rotating seven-day service.
verses.before: Their kin who lived in their settlements were to come in with them for seven days at a time.
verses.after: Their relatives in the villages came at appointed times to work with them for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their kin who lived in their settlements were to come in with them for seven days at a time.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the permanent chiefs’ custodial responsibilities.
verses.before: For the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God.
verses.after: The four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, held positions of trust. They oversaw the chambers and treasuries of God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God.

verses.rationale: Make the reason for their lodging clear.
verses.before: They spent the nights around the house of God, because the guard duty was theirs; they were responsible for opening it morning by morning.
verses.after: They spent the night around God’s house, because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: They spent the nights around the house of God, because the guard duty was theirs; they were responsible for opening it morning by morning.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated inventory practice.
verses.before: Some of them were responsible for the utensils of the service, for they brought them in by count and took them out by count.
verses.after: Some were responsible for the articles used in worship. They counted them when bringing them in and when taking them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of them were responsible for the utensils of the service, for they brought them in by count and took them out by count.

verses.rationale: Keep every category of material entrusted to them.
verses.before: Others of them were appointed over the vessels and all the holy utensils, and over the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
verses.after: Others were appointed over the furnishings and all the sacred utensils, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Others of them were appointed over the vessels and all the holy utensils, and over the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.

verses.rationale: Preserve the distinction between priestly preparation and Levitical custody.
verses.before: Some of the priests’ descendants prepared the ointment of spices.
verses.after: Some of the priests blended the spices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of the priests’ descendants prepared the ointment of spices.

verses.rationale: Keep the specific food preparation and his lineage.
verses.before: Mattithiah, one of the Levites—the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite—was entrusted with the work of preparing the baked offerings.
verses.after: Mattithiah, a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with preparing the griddle cakes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mattithiah, one of the Levites—the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite—was entrusted with the work of preparing the baked offerings.

verses.rationale: Retain the weekly rhythm and the bread’s arrangement.
verses.before: Some of the Kohathites, from among their kin, were responsible for the bread set out in rows, preparing it Sabbath by Sabbath.
verses.after: Some of their Kohathite relatives were responsible for preparing the arranged bread every Sabbath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of the Kohathites, from among their kin, were responsible for the bread set out in rows, preparing it Sabbath by Sabbath.

verses.rationale: Explain the exemption in relation to continuous musical service.
verses.before: These were the singers, heads of ancestral houses of the Levites. They lived in the rooms and were free from other duties, because the work was upon them day and night.
verses.after: The singers, heads of Levitical households, stayed in the chambers and were free from other duties, because their work occupied them day and night.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were the singers, heads of ancestral houses of the Levites. They lived in the rooms and were free from other duties, because the work was upon them day and night.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated leadership summary and residence.
verses.before: These were heads of ancestral houses of the Levites, according to their generations—chiefs. They lived in Jerusalem.
verses.after: These were the heads of Levitical ancestral households, leaders listed by their generations. They lived in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were heads of ancestral houses of the Levites, according to their generations—chiefs. They lived in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Follow the read Jeiel, named here but absent from 8:29.
verses.before: In Gibeon lived Jeiel, the father of Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah,
verses.after: Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In Gibeon lived Jeiel, the father of Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah,

verses.rationale: Retain Ner’s presence in this list.
verses.before: and his firstborn son was Abdon; then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,
verses.after: His firstborn son was Abdon; then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
verses.tsw_comparator: and his firstborn son was Abdon; then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,

verses.rationale: Keep Zechariah and Mikloth in this version of the family list.
verses.before: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
verses.after: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

verses.rationale: Retain Shimeam here alongside Shimeah in chapter 8.
verses.before: Mikloth fathered Shimeam. They also lived near their kin in Jerusalem, alongside their kin.
verses.after: Mikloth fathered Shimeam. They too lived in Jerusalem with their relatives, opposite their relatives’ homes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mikloth fathered Shimeam. They also lived near their kin in Jerusalem, alongside their kin.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated genealogy linking the book to Saul’s story.
verses.before: Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul; Saul fathered Jonathan, Malkishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
verses.after: Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul. Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul; Saul fathered Jonathan, Malkishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

verses.rationale: Keep the same person’s name despite the shortened written second form.
verses.before: Jonathan’s son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
verses.after: Jonathan’s son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan’s son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.

verses.rationale: Retain three names here rather than inserting Ahaz from chapter 8.
verses.before: The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.
verses.after: Micah’s sons were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.

verses.rationale: Keep Jarah as this record names him.
verses.before: Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.
verses.after: Ahaz fathered Jarah. Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri fathered Moza.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.

verses.rationale: Retain Rephaiah rather than harmonizing to Raphah.
verses.before: Moza fathered Binea; his son was Rephaiah, his son Eleasah, and his son Azel.
verses.after: Moza fathered Binea. His line continued through Rephaiah, then Eleasah, then Azel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moza fathered Binea; his son was Rephaiah, his son Eleasah, and his son Azel.

verses.rationale: Close the repeated family record with all six names.
verses.before: Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.
verses.after: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel’s sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

verses.rationale: Keep flight and deaths in the opening defeat.
verses.before: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
verses.after: The Philistines fought against Israel. Israel’s men fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Name all three sons killed in the pursuit.
verses.before: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-shua, Saul’s sons.
verses.after: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons. They killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-shua, Saul’s sons.

verses.rationale: Retain the verb’s fear sense with the possible wounded reading noted.
verses.before: The battle bore heavily upon Saul, and the archers found him. He was in anguish because of the archers.
verses.after: The battle closed in on Saul. The archers found him, and he trembled before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The battle bore heavily upon Saul, and the archers found him. He was in anguish because of the archers.

verses.rationale: Preserve Saul’s stated fear and the sequence of refusals and actions.
verses.before: Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer would not, for he was very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
verses.after: Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through, so these uncircumcised men won’t come and abuse me.” His armor-bearer was too afraid to do it. So Saul took his sword and fell on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer would not, for he was very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.

verses.rationale: Keep the second death and its immediate cause.
verses.before: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell upon the sword and died.
verses.after: When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died.
verses.tsw_comparator: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell upon the sword and died.

verses.rationale: Retain Chronicles’ comprehensive house statement without silently reconciling other survivors.
verses.before: Thus Saul died, along with his three sons; all his house died together.
verses.after: Saul and his three sons died; his whole house died together.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Saul died, along with his three sons; all his house died together.

verses.rationale: Make the chain from military defeat to civilian displacement clear.
verses.before: When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and lived in them.
verses.after: When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had fled and Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. The Philistines came and occupied them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and lived in them.

verses.rationale: Retain the stripping of the dead and location.
verses.before: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.after: The next day the Philistines came to strip the slain and found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Keep both human and cultic recipients of the victory news.
verses.before: They stripped him and took away his head and his weapons. They sent them throughout the land of the Philistines, to bring the news to their idols and to the people.
verses.after: They stripped Saul and took his head and armor. They sent word throughout Philistine territory, announcing the news to their idols and their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They stripped him and took away his head and his weapons. They sent them throughout the land of the Philistines, to bring the news to their idols and to the people.

verses.rationale: Preserve the treatment of the body and distinct temple references.
verses.before: They placed his weapons in the house of their gods, and they fastened his skull in the house of Dagon.
verses.after: They placed his armor in their gods’ temple and fastened his skull in Dagon’s temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: They placed his weapons in the house of their gods, and they fastened his skull in the house of Dagon.

verses.rationale: Let the report lead naturally into the rescue of the bodies.
verses.before: When all Jabesh-gilead heard everything that the Philistines had done to Saul,
verses.after: When everyone in Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
verses.tsw_comparator: When all Jabesh-gilead heard everything that the Philistines had done to Saul,

verses.rationale: Retain the tree species and seven-day mourning without importing details from Samuel.
verses.before: all the valiant men rose up and carried away Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons. They brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones beneath the oak in Jabesh. Then they fasted seven days.
verses.after: all their warriors set out, recovered Saul’s body and his sons’ bodies, and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones beneath the terebinth there and fasted for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the valiant men rose up and carried away Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons. They brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones beneath the oak in Jabesh. Then they fasted seven days.

verses.rationale: Keep the narrator’s explicit grounds for judgment.
verses.before: So Saul died because of his unfaithfulness that he committed against the LORD: because of the word of the LORD that he did not keep, and also because he consulted a medium to seek guidance.
verses.after: Saul died because of his unfaithfulness to the LORD: he had not kept the LORD’s word, and he had consulted a medium for guidance.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul died because of his unfaithfulness that he committed against the LORD: because of the word of the LORD that he did not keep, and also because he consulted a medium to seek guidance.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine agency alongside the narrated suicide.
verses.before: He did not seek the LORD, so he put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
verses.after: He did not seek the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did not seek the LORD, so he put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.

verses.rationale: Keep the embodied kinship expression.
verses.before: Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.
verses.after: All Israel gathered around David at Hebron and said, “We are your own bone and flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.

verses.rationale: Retain shepherding as the image of kingship.
verses.before: In times past, even when Saul was king, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing them in. And the LORD your God said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be leader over my people Israel.’”
verses.after: Even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. The LORD your God told you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel and be ruler over them.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: In times past, even when Saul was king, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing them in. And the LORD your God said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be leader over my people Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Keep covenant, anointing, and Samuel’s mediation distinct.
verses.before: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel.
verses.after: All Israel’s elders came to the king at Hebron. David made a covenant with them there before the LORD, and they anointed him king over Israel, as the LORD had said through Samuel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel.

verses.rationale: Preserve both city names and its inhabitants.
verses.before: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem—that is, Jebus—where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were.
verses.after: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites lived.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem—that is, Jebus—where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were.

verses.rationale: Keep the challenge and reversal without importing Samuel’s different speech.
verses.before: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here.” But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the City of David.
verses.after: The people of Jebus told David, “You will not get in here.” But David captured the stronghold of Zion, now the City of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here.” But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the City of David.

verses.rationale: Retain the condition and Joab’s advancement.
verses.before: David said, “Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first will become chief and commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.
verses.after: David had said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first will become chief and commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first will become chief and commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.

verses.rationale: Keep the explanation of the city’s name.
verses.before: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of David.
verses.after: David settled in the stronghold, so it was called the City of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of David.

verses.rationale: Retain the division of construction work and the ancient Millo term.
verses.before: He built up the city all around, from the Millo and all around it; and Joab restored the rest of the city.
verses.after: He built up the city all around, from the Millo outward. Joab restored the rest of the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built up the city all around, from the Millo and all around it; and Joab restored the rest of the city.

verses.rationale: Preserve the continuing increase and divine title.
verses.before: David became greater and greater, for LORD of Hosts was with him.
verses.after: David grew more and more powerful, and the LORD of Armies was with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David became greater and greater, for LORD of Hosts was with him.

verses.rationale: Keep the warriors and all Israel as joint supporters.
verses.before: These are the chiefs of David’s warriors, who gave him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.
verses.after: These were the heads of David’s mighty warriors. Together with all Israel, they gave him strong support in establishing his kingdom, making him king as the LORD had spoken concerning Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the chiefs of David’s warriors, who gave him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve the three-hundred count and note the difficult rank title.
verses.before: This is the number of David’s warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty. He raised his spear against three hundred slain at one time.
verses.after: This is the roll of David’s mighty warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Three, raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them in a single encounter.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the number of David’s warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty. He raised his spear against three hundred slain at one time.

verses.rationale: Keep his ancestry and membership in the Three.
verses.before: After him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he was among the three warriors.
verses.after: Next was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he was among the three warriors.

verses.rationale: Retain barley and this account’s actors rather than importing Samuel’s field story.
verses.before: He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was a portion of the field full of barley, and the people fled from before the Philistines.
verses.after: He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was a field full of barley, and the people fled before the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was a portion of the field full of barley, and the people fled from before the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keep the plural defenders and divine attribution.
verses.before: But they took their stand in the middle of the field and defended it, and struck down the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance.
verses.after: They took their stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. The LORD brought about a great victory.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they took their stand in the middle of the field and defended it, and struck down the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance.

verses.rationale: Retain the three-from-thirty distinction and both settings.
verses.before: Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock, at the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine camp was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: Three of the thirty leading warriors went down to David at the rock near the cave of Adullam. A Philistine force was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock, at the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine camp was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Set the danger behind David’s wish.
verses.before: David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was then in Bethlehem.
verses.after: David was then in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was then in Bethlehem.

verses.rationale: Express the wish naturally while retaining its specific source.
verses.before: David longed and said, “Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate?”
verses.after: David longed for water and said, “If only someone would bring me a drink from the cistern by Bethlehem’s gate!”
verses.tsw_comparator: David longed and said, “Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate?”

verses.rationale: Keep the dangerous retrieval and offering of the water.
verses.before: So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate, carried it, and brought it to David. But David would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.
verses.after: The three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the cistern by Bethlehem’s gate, and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it and poured it out to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate, carried it, and brought it to David. But David would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain the blood-and-life image and repeated refusal.
verses.before: He said, “Far be it from me, before my God, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men—their lives? For they brought it at the risk of their lives.” Therefore he would not drink it. These things the three warriors did.
verses.after: “My God forbid that I should do this!” he said. “Could I drink these men’s blood at the cost of their lives? They brought it at the risk of their lives.” He would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three mighty warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Far be it from me, before my God, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men—their lives? For they brought it at the risk of their lives.” Therefore he would not drink it. These things the three warriors did.

verses.rationale: Follow the read positive renown clause and retain the rank tension.
verses.before: Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the three. He raised his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the three.
verses.after: Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them, gaining a name among the Three.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the three. He raised his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the three.

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult twice/three wording without replacing a group number.
verses.before: Among the three, he was more honored than the two, and he became their commander; but he did not attain to the three.
verses.after: He was twice as honored as the Three and became their commander, though he did not attain to the Three.
verses.tsw_comparator: Among the three, he was more honored than the two, and he became their commander; but he did not attain to the three.

verses.rationale: Retain ariels as an uncertain source term explained in a note.

verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, a man of many deeds. He struck down Moab’s two ariels. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

verses.rationale: Preserve height, implements, and the reversal of weapons.
verses.before: He struck down an Egyptian, a man five cubits tall. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand like a weaver’s beam, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
verses.after: He killed an Egyptian five cubits tall whose spear was like a weaver’s beam. Benaiah went down against him with a staff, seized the spear from his hand, and killed him with his own spear.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck down an Egyptian, a man five cubits tall. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand like a weaver’s beam, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.

verses.rationale: Keep the renown formula and full name.

verses.after: These were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and they gave him a name among the three mighty warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three warriors.

verses.rationale: Keep the exile-like restriction and the men’s military role.

verses.tsw_comparator: These are those who came to David at Ziklag, while he was still kept back because of Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who helped in battle:

verses.rationale: Preserve their ambidextrous skill and connection to Saul.
verses.before: armed with bows, able to use the right hand and the left with stones and arrows from the bow. They were from Saul’s kindred, from Benjamin:

verses.tsw_comparator: armed with bows, able to use the right hand and the left with stones and arrows from the bow. They were from Saul’s kindred, from Benjamin:

verses.rationale: Follow the read Jeziel and keep the two sibling groups distinct.

verses.after: Ahiezer the chief, and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahiezer was the chief, and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite;

verses.rationale: Combine the two complete Hebrew records belonging to this public label.
verses.before: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a warrior among the Thirty and over the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;
verses.after: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a warrior among the Thirty and a leader over them; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad the Gederathite;
verses.tsw_comparator: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a warrior among the Thirty and over the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;

verses.before: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite;
verses.after: Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite;

verses.after: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;

verses.rationale: Preserve both animal images and the voluntary separation.

verses.after: Some Gadites separated themselves to join David at the wilderness stronghold. They were mighty warriors, trained for battle with shield and spear, with faces like lions and speed like gazelles on the mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the Gadites, some separated themselves to David at the wilderness stronghold: mighty warriors, men of war, equipped with shield and spear; their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were swift as gazelles on the mountains.

verses.after: Ezer was chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,

verses.rationale: Retain the capacity reading while noting the alternative command-size reading.

verses.rationale: Keep the seasonal flood and displacement on both sides.

verses.tsw_comparator: These were the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it overflowed all its banks, and they put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.

verses.rationale: Retain both tribal sources.

verses.tsw_comparator: Some of the Benjaminites and Judeans came to David at the stronghold.

verses.rationale: Preserve David’s condition, innocence claim, and appeal to judgment.
verses.before: David went out to meet them and answered them: “If you have come to me in peace, to help me, my heart will be united with you. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, though there is no violence in my hands, may the God of our ancestors see it and rebuke you.”
verses.after: David went out to meet them. “If you have come in peace to help me, my heart will be united with yours,” he said. “But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, though my hands have done no violence, may the God of our ancestors see and judge.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David went out to meet them and answered them: “If you have come to me in peace, to help me, my heart will be united with you. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, though there is no violence in my hands, may the God of our ancestors see it and rebuke you.”

verses.rationale: Keep the clothing image, repeated peace, and poetic pledge within the verse.
verses.before: Then the spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty: To you, David, and with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to people who help you, for your God helps you. So David received them and made them leaders of the raiding bands.
verses.after: Then the Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty: “Yours, David! With you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, for your God helps you.” David welcomed them and made them leaders of his troops.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty: To you, David, and with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, for your God helps you. So David received them and made them leaders of the raiding bands.

verses.rationale: Keep the Philistine leaders’ stated calculation and threat to themselves.
verses.before: Some from Manasseh joined David when he went with the Philistines against Saul for battle, though they did not help them. For the rulers of the Philistines, after taking counsel, sent him away, saying, “At the cost of our heads he will fall away to his lord Saul.”
verses.after: Some from Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight Saul. But he did not help the Philistines, because their rulers conferred and sent him away: “He will defect to his master Saul at the cost of our heads.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Some from Manasseh joined David when he went with the Philistines against Saul for battle, though they did not help them. For the rulers of the Philistines, after taking counsel, sent him away, saying, “At the cost of our heads he will fall away to his lord Saul.”

verses.before: From Zebulun, people who went out for military service, arraying themselves for battle with every kind of weapon of war: fifty thousand, ready to give support without a divided heart.
verses.after: From Zebulun: fifty thousand ready for service, prepared for battle with every kind of weapon, able to keep ranks with undivided hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Zebulun, those who went out for military service, arraying themselves for battle with every kind of weapon of war: fifty thousand, ready to give support without a divided heart.

verses.rationale: Distinguish commanders from the larger armed force.
verses.before: From Naphtali: one thousand commanders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.
verses.after: From Naphtali: a thousand commanders, with thirty-seven thousand men carrying shield and spear.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Naphtali: one thousand commanders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.

verses.rationale: Keep the exact tribal total.
verses.before: From the Danites, arrayed for battle: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
verses.after: From Dan: 28,600 prepared for battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the Danites, arrayed for battle: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.

verses.rationale: Retain both readiness descriptions.
verses.before: From Asher, people who went out for military service, to array themselves for battle: forty thousand.
verses.after: From Asher: forty thousand ready for military service and battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Asher, those who went out for military service, to array themselves for battle: forty thousand.

verses.rationale: Keep the eastern tribes together and the combined total.
verses.before: From beyond the Jordan, from the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, equipped with every weapon of war: one hundred twenty thousand.
verses.after: From across the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh: one hundred twenty thousand with every kind of weapon.
verses.tsw_comparator: From beyond the Jordan, from the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, equipped with every weapon of war: one hundred twenty thousand.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated heart language and the all-Israel emphasis.
verses.before: All these men of war, arrayed in battle formation, came to Hebron with a whole heart to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of Israel also had one heart to make David king.
verses.after: All these fighting men, able to keep their ranks, came to Hebron wholeheartedly to make David king over all Israel. The rest of Israel too was of one heart in making David king.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these men of war, arrayed in battle formation, came to Hebron with a whole heart to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of Israel also had one heart to make David king.

verses.rationale: Retain the three-day feast and relatives’ support.
verses.before: They were there with David for three days, eating and drinking, for their kindred had prepared provisions for them.
verses.after: They stayed with David for three days, eating and drinking, because their relatives had prepared supplies for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They were there with David for three days, eating and drinking, for their kindred had prepared provisions for them.

verses.rationale: Keep every transport and food category and the joyful conclusion.
verses.before: Also those near them, as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and cattle: flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance. For there was joy in Israel.
verses.after: Their neighbors, even as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen: flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, oil, and cattle and flocks in abundance. There was joy in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also those near them, as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and cattle: flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance. For there was joy in Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the consultation with leaders at both military levels.
verses.before: David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.
verses.after: David consulted the commanders of thousands and hundreds and all the other leaders.
verses.tsw_comparator: David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

verses.rationale: Preserve the two conditions and the inclusion of rural priestly and Levitical settlements.
verses.before: Then David said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is from the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to our kindred who remain in all the lands of Israel, and with them to the priests and Levites in their towns and pasturelands, that they may gather to us.
verses.after: Then he said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If this seems good to you and is from the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to our relatives who remain throughout Israel, including the priests and Levites in their towns with pasturelands, asking them to join us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is from the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to our kindred who remain in all the lands of Israel, and with them to the priests and Levites in their towns and pasturelands, that they may gather to us.

verses.rationale: Retain the ark as the immediate object of seeking without erasing the wider religious implication.
verses.before: Let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul.”
verses.after: Let us bring the ark of our God back to us. We did not seek it out in Saul’s time.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul.”

verses.rationale: Make the shared approval clear without adding divine endorsement.

verses.after: The whole assembly agreed to do this, because the proposal seemed right to all the people.

verses.rationale: Keep the named territorial limits and the ark’s starting point.

verses.after: So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath-jearim.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.

verses.rationale: Unfold the divine titles while retaining the ark’s association with the Name.
verses.before: David and all Israel went up to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD, who sits enthroned above the cherubim—the ark called by the Name.
verses.after: David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim in Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD enthroned above the cherubim, the ark called by his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and all Israel went up to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD, who sits enthroned above the cherubim—the ark called by the Name.

verses.rationale: Keep the new cart and both drivers without anticipating the later carrying rule.
verses.before: They set the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab. Uzzah and Ahio were driving the cart.
verses.after: They carried God’s ark on a new cart from Abinadab’s house. Uzza and Ahio guided the cart.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab. Uzzah and Ahio were driving the cart.

verses.rationale: Preserve the full instrument list and wholehearted celebration.

verses.after: David and all Israel celebrated before God with all their strength, with songs, lyres, harps, drums, cymbals, and trumpets.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their strength, with songs and with lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

verses.rationale: Keep the named location and the physical reason for reaching out.
verses.before: When they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to hold the ark, because the cattle stumbled.
verses.after: When they reached Chidon’s threshing floor, Uzza reached out to steady the ark, because the oxen stumbled.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to hold the ark, because the cattle stumbled.

verses.rationale: Preserve the narrated cause, divine agency, and death without softening them.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and he struck him because he had reached out his hand against the ark. He died there before God.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Uzza. He struck him down because he had reached out his hand to the ark, and Uzza died there before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and he struck him because he had reached out his hand against the ark. He died there before God.

verses.rationale: Keep David’s anger and the repeated breaking-out language behind the name.
verses.before: David was angry because the LORD had burst out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, as it is to this day.
verses.after: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzza. He called that place Perez-uzza, its name to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was angry because the LORD had burst out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, as it is to this day.

verses.rationale: Retain the movement from anger to fear and David’s question.
verses.before: David feared God that day, saying, “How can I bring the ark of God to me?”
verses.after: David was afraid of God that day. “How can I bring God’s ark to me?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: David feared God that day, saying, “How can I bring the ark of God to me?”

verses.rationale: Clarify the changed destination and preserve the Gittite designation.
verses.before: So David did not bring the ark to himself, to the City of David, but turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.after: David did not take the ark home to the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David did not bring the ark to himself, to the City of David, but turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

verses.rationale: Retain the household repetition, duration, and comprehensive blessing.

verses.after: God’s ark stayed with Obed-edom’s household, in his house, for three months. The LORD blessed Obed-edom’s household and everything he had.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that belonged to him.

verses.rationale: Follow the read form Huram and preserve the craftsmen’s distinct trades.
verses.before: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, masons, and woodworkers, to build him a house.
verses.after: Huram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, stoneworkers, and woodworkers, to build him a house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, masons, and woodworkers, to build him a house.

verses.rationale: Keep the people’s welfare as the stated reason for royal elevation.
verses.before: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom had been exalted greatly for the sake of his people Israel.
verses.after: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had raised his kingdom high for the sake of his people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom had been exalted greatly for the sake of his people Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain the additional marriages and both sons and daughters.
verses.before: David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David fathered more sons and daughters.
verses.after: In Jerusalem David took more wives, and he fathered more sons and daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David fathered more sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Keep the opening four names and let the list continue across verse labels.
verses.before: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;
verses.after: These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;

verses.rationale: Preserve these forms rather than harmonizing the earlier genealogy.
verses.before: Ibhar, Elishua, and Elpelet;
verses.after: Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ibhar, Elishua, and Elpelet;

verses.rationale: Retain all three names in order.
verses.before: Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia;
verses.after: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
verses.tsw_comparator: Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia;

verses.rationale: Keep Beeliada and distinguish Eliphelet from Elpelet in verse 5.
verses.before: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
verses.after: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.

verses.rationale: Preserve the all-Israel kingship and the opposing movements.
verses.before: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went out before them.
verses.after: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went up to seek him out. David heard about it and went out to face them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went out before them.

verses.rationale: Retain the valley’s name and the raiding action.
verses.before: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: The Philistines came and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Keep both questions and the repeated hand image in the assurance.
verses.before: David inquired of God, saying, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD said to him, “Go up, and I will give them into your hand.”
verses.after: David asked God, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD answered him, “Go up. I will give them into your hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David inquired of God, saying, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD said to him, “Go up, and I will give them into your hand.”

verses.rationale: Retain the water image and the breaking-through wordplay.
verses.before: So they went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there. David said, “God has burst through my enemies by my hand, like a bursting flood.” Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
verses.after: They went up to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like water bursting through.” That is why they named the place Baal-perazim.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there. David said, “God has burst through my enemies by my hand, like a bursting flood.” Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.

verses.rationale: Keep the destruction of the abandoned gods and David’s command.
verses.before: They left their gods there, and David gave the command, and they were burned with fire.
verses.after: The Philistines left their gods there, and David ordered them burned.
verses.tsw_comparator: They left their gods there, and David gave the command, and they were burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserve the renewed raid without importing details from Samuel.
verses.before: Again the Philistines spread out in the valley.
verses.after: Once again the Philistines raided the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again the Philistines spread out in the valley.

verses.rationale: Retain the changed strategy and the uncertain tree identification in an accessible term.
verses.before: David again inquired of God, and God said to him, “You must not go up after them. Circle around from behind them, and come against them opposite the baca trees.
verses.after: David asked God again, and God told him, “Do not go up after them. Circle around them and approach them opposite the balsam trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: David again inquired of God, and God said to him, “You must not go up after them. Circle around from behind them, and come against them opposite the baca trees.

verses.rationale: Preserve the audible sign and God’s preceding action.
verses.before: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the baca trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”
verses.after: When you hear the sound of marching in the treetops, go out to battle. God will have gone out ahead of you to strike the Philistine camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the baca trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Keep Gibeon as Chronicles gives it rather than substituting Samuel’s place-name.
verses.before: David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the camp of the Philistines from Gibeon as far as Gezer.
verses.after: David did as God commanded. They struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon to Gezer.
verses.tsw_comparator: David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the camp of the Philistines from Gibeon as far as Gezer.

verses.rationale: Retain the broad geographical reach and the LORD’s agency.
verses.before: David’s name went out through all the lands, and the LORD put fear of him on all the nations.
verses.after: David’s fame spread through all the lands, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s name went out through all the lands, and the LORD put fear of him on all the nations.

verses.rationale: Distinguish David’s houses from the prepared tent for the ark.
verses.before: David made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
verses.after: David built houses for himself in the City of David. He prepared a place for God’s ark and pitched a tent for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: David made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

verses.rationale: Preserve the restriction, divine choice, and continuing service.
verses.before: Then David said, “No one is to carry the ark of God except the Levites, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister to him forever.”
verses.after: Then David said, “Only the Levites may carry God’s ark. The LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David said, “No one is to carry the ark of God except the Levites, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister to him forever.”

verses.rationale: Keep the national assembly and the prepared destination.
verses.before: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to its place, which he had prepared for it.
verses.after: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring the ark of the LORD up to the place he had prepared for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to its place, which he had prepared for it.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the Aaronic family within the gathering and introduce the roster.
verses.before: David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
verses.after: He gathered Aaron’s descendants and the Levites:
verses.tsw_comparator: David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:

verses.rationale: Keep the named leader and exact count.

verses.after: from Kohath’s descendants, Uriel the leader and 120 of his relatives;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and one hundred twenty of his kindred;

verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and two hundred twenty of his kindred;

verses.after: from Gershom’s descendants, Joel the leader and 130 of his relatives;

verses.rationale: Keep this family listed separately from the broader ancestral divisions.

verses.after: from Elizaphan’s descendants, Shemaiah the leader and 200 of his relatives;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and two hundred of his kindred;

verses.rationale: Preserve the family name and count.
verses.before: from the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and eighty of his kindred;
verses.after: from Hebron’s descendants, Eliel the leader and 80 of his relatives;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and eighty of his kindred;

verses.rationale: Retain the final group’s precise number.
verses.before: from the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and one hundred twelve of his kindred.
verses.after: from Uzziel’s descendants, Amminadab the leader and 112 of his relatives.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and one hundred twelve of his kindred.

verses.rationale: Retain consecration and make the leaders’ responsibility explicit.

verses.rationale: Supply the carrying action implicit in the broken Hebrew clause and retain collective responsibility.
verses.before: Because you were not there at the first, the LORD our God broke out against us, for we did not seek him according to the ordinance.”
verses.after: Because you did not carry it the first time, the LORD our God broke out against us. We did not seek him in the prescribed way.”

verses.rationale: Keep both groups and the purpose of their consecration.

verses.after: So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
