verses.rationale: Preserve the separate roster and technical musical term.
verses.before: Mattithiah, Eliphlehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to play lyres according to the eighth, to lead.
verses.after: Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead with lyres according to sheminith.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mattithiah, Eliphlehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to play lyres according to the eighth, to lead.

verses.rationale: Choose the musical reading of massa in context while marking its carrying alternative in a note.
verses.before: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites for the carrying, directed the carrying, because he was skillful.
verses.after: Chenaniah, the Levites’ leader in music, directed the music because he understood it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites for the carrying, directed the carrying, because he was skillful.

verses.rationale: Keep the ark-specific gatekeeping duty.
verses.before: Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
verses.after: Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.

verses.rationale: Preserve all seven priests and Jehiah’s distinct name.
verses.before: Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer the priests were sounding trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.
verses.after: The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were to sound trumpets before God’s ark. Obed-edom and Jehiah were also gatekeepers for the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer the priests were sounding trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.

verses.rationale: Retain covenant terminology and all three leadership groups.
verses.before: David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom with joy.
verses.after: David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with joy to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant up from Obed-edom’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom with joy.

verses.rationale: Keep the stated reason and both exact sacrificial counts.
verses.before: And when God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
verses.after: Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD’s covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the shared robe from David’s additional ephod and retain the musical reading consistently.
verses.before: David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, the leader of the carrying, among the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.
verses.after: David wore a robe of fine linen, as did all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, the leader of the singers’ music. David also wore a linen ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, the leader of the carrying, among the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.

verses.rationale: Keep every sound and instrument in the procession.
verses.before: Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with a shout, with the sound of the ram’s horn, with trumpets and cymbals sounding, and with harps and lyres.
verses.after: All Israel brought up the ark of the LORD’s covenant with shouts, the sound of the ram’s horn, trumpets and cymbals, and music from harps and lyres.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with a shout, with the sound of the ram’s horn, with trumpets and cymbals sounding, and with harps and lyres.

verses.rationale: Keep Michal identified as Saul’s daughter and end with her inward response without importing Samuel’s dialogue.
verses.before: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked out through the window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
verses.after: As the ark of the LORD’s covenant entered the City of David, Michal, Saul’s daughter, looked down through a window. She saw King David leaping and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked out through the window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.

verses.rationale: Retain both offering categories and the tent setting.
verses.before: They brought in the ark of God and set it within the tent that David had pitched for it, and they presented burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before God.
verses.after: They brought God’s ark in and set it inside the tent David had pitched for it. Then they presented burnt offerings and well-being offerings before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought in the ark of God and set it within the tent that David had pitched for it, and they presented burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before God.

verses.rationale: Keep the blessing after the offerings and its divine-name formula.
verses.before: When David had finished presenting the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
verses.after: When David finished presenting the burnt offerings and well-being offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: When David had finished presenting the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve equal distribution to women and men while noting the uncertain middle food item.
verses.before: He distributed to every Israelite, to each man and woman, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
verses.after: He distributed food to every Israelite, man and woman alike: a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake for each.
verses.tsw_comparator: He distributed to every Israelite, to each man and woman, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.

verses.rationale: Retain three distinct actions rather than collapsing them into worship.
verses.before: He appointed some of the Levites to serve before the ark of the LORD, to call to remembrance, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:
verses.after: He appointed some Levites to serve before the ark of the LORD, to commemorate, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He appointed some of the Levites to serve before the ark of the LORD, to call to remembrance, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:

verses.rationale: Keep both occurrences of Jeiel and distinguish Asaph’s instrument.
verses.before: Asaph the leader; Zechariah second to him; Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; and Asaph sounding the cymbals.
verses.after: Asaph was the leader, with Zechariah second, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They played harps and lyres, while Asaph sounded the cymbals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Asaph the leader; Zechariah second to him; Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; and Asaph sounding the cymbals.

verses.rationale: Keep the two priests and continuing duty.
verses.before: Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were continually with trumpets before the ark of the covenant of God.
verses.after: The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel sounded trumpets regularly before the ark of God’s covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were continually with trumpets before the ark of the covenant of God.

verses.rationale: Marks the inauguration of thanksgiving under Asaph without claiming that David composed the following song; clears the nested entrusting clauses.
verses.before: On that day David first assigned Asaph and his kindred to give thanks to the LORD:
verses.after: That day David first charged Asaph and his relatives with giving thanks to the LORD:
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day David first assigned Asaph and his kindred to give thanks to the LORD:

verses.rationale: Preserve the parallel commands and public witness.
verses.before: Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name; reveal his deeds among the peoples.
verses.after: Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name. Make his deeds known among the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name; make known his deeds among the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keep both musical commands and the comprehensive wonders.
verses.before: Sing to him; make music to him; speak of all his wonderful works.
verses.after: Sing to him; make music to him. Tell of all his wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to him; make music to him; speak of all his wonderful works.

verses.rationale: Retain boasting directed toward the Name and the seeking theme.
verses.before: Glory in his holy name; let the heart of people who seek the LORD rejoice.
verses.after: Boast in his holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Glory in his holy name; let the heart of those who seek the LORD rejoice.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated seeking and the ancient face image.
verses.before: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face continually.
verses.after: Seek the LORD and his strength. Seek his face continually.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face continually.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three objects of remembering and the mouth image.
verses.before: Remember his wonderful works that he has done, his signs and the judgments of his mouth,
verses.after: Remember the wonders he has done, his signs and the judgments from his mouth,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember his wonderful works that he has done, his signs and the judgments of his mouth,

verses.rationale: Retain Israel rather than substituting the parallel psalm’s Abraham.
verses.before: offspring of Israel, his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
verses.after: you offspring of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: offspring of Israel, his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones.

verses.rationale: Keep the confession and worldwide judicial scope.
verses.before: He is the LORD, our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
verses.after: He is the LORD our God. His judgments reach all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the LORD, our God; his judgments are in all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain the imperative to remember and the exact thousand generations.
verses.before: Remember forever his covenant, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
verses.after: Remember his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember forever his covenant, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,

verses.rationale: Make the covenant referent explicit while retaining the paired ancestors.
verses.before: the covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
verses.after: the covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: the covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.

verses.rationale: Preserve decree and covenant as parallel descriptions.
verses.before: He established it for Jacob as a statute, for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
verses.after: He established it for Jacob as a decree, for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: He established it for Jacob as a statute, for Israel as an everlasting covenant,

verses.rationale: Retain the named land and inheritance image.
verses.before: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance,”
verses.after: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, your allotted inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance,”

verses.rationale: Keep the second-person address and repeated smallness.
verses.before: when you were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.
verses.after: When you were few in number, very few, and living there as foreigners,
verses.tsw_comparator: when you were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.

verses.rationale: Preserve the shift to third person and both parallel movements.
verses.before: They went from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
verses.after: they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.

verses.rationale: Keep divine protection and the rebuke introducing quoted speech.
verses.before: He allowed no one to oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:
verses.after: He allowed no one to oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:
verses.tsw_comparator: He allowed no one to oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:

verses.rationale: Retain plural anointed ones and prophets without narrowing them to later offices.
verses.before: “Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.”
verses.after: “Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the worldwide address and repeated daily proclamation.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim from day to day his salvation.
verses.after: Sing to the LORD, all the earth. Tell the good news of his salvation day after day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim from day to day his salvation.

verses.rationale: Keep the two parallel objects and audiences.
verses.before: Tell among the nations his glory, among all the peoples his wonderful works.
verses.after: Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell among the nations his glory, among all the peoples his wonderful works.

verses.rationale: Retain the comparison with all gods and the language of fear.
verses.before: For great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.after: For the LORD is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: For great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.rationale: Preserve the polemical contrast and creation claim.
verses.before: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
verses.after: All the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retain joy here rather than harmonizing the parallel psalm.
verses.before: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his place.
verses.after: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated liturgical command and family grouping of peoples.
verses.before: Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
verses.after: Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three commands and leave the holiness phrase broad, with its alternative noted.
verses.before: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in holy splendor.
verses.after: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name. Bring an offering and come before him. Bow before the LORD in holy splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in holy splendor.

verses.rationale: Retain trembling beside the world’s stability.
verses.before: Tremble before him, all the earth. Indeed, the world is established; it will not be shaken.
verses.after: Tremble before him, all the earth. The world stands firm; it will not be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tremble before him, all the earth. Indeed, the world is established; it will not be shaken.

verses.rationale: Preserve the cosmic joy and royal proclamation.
verses.before: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!”
verses.after: Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad. Let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!”

verses.rationale: Keep the nonhuman creation’s own voiced response.
verses.before: Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the field exult, and everything in it.
verses.after: Let the sea roar, and everything in it. Let the fields rejoice, and everything in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the field exult, and everything in it.

verses.rationale: Retain the trees’ celebration and judgment as the stated reason.
verses.before: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
verses.after: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated thanksgiving formula and enduring covenantal love.
verses.before: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love is forever.
verses.after: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love is forever.

verses.rationale: Preserve the petition for gathering and rescue without relocating its historical voice.
verses.before: And say, “Save us, God of our salvation; gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.”
verses.after: Say, “Save us, God of our salvation. Gather us and rescue us from the nations, so we may thank your holy name and glory in praising you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And say, “Save us, God of our salvation; gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.”

verses.rationale: Mark the people’s response as narrative after the blessing while keeping all text within its verse paragraph.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. And all the people said, “Amen!” and praised the LORD.
verses.after: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Then all the people said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. And all the people said, “Amen!” and praised the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the continuing daily service at the ark.
verses.before: So he left there, before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, Asaph and his kindred, to serve continually before the ark, according to the matter required each day;
verses.after: David left Asaph and his relatives there before the ark of the LORD’s covenant to serve regularly before the ark, attending to each day’s needs.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he left there, before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, Asaph and his kindred, to serve continually before the ark, according to the matter required each day;

verses.rationale: Preserve the plural their and the repeated Obed-edom without deciding whether two people are meant.
verses.before: and Obed-edom and their kindred, sixty-eight of them; also Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
verses.after: He also left Obed-edom and their sixty-eight relatives. Obed-edom son of Jedithun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Obed-edom and their kindred, sixty-eight of them; also Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the Gibeon tabernacle from the ark’s Jerusalem tent.
verses.before: He left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon,
verses.after: He left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the LORD’s tabernacle at the high place in Gibeon,
verses.tsw_comparator: He left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon,

verses.rationale: Preserve the twice-daily rhythm and the written instruction’s authority.
verses.before: to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the instruction of the LORD, which he commanded Israel.
verses.after: to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, following everything written in the instruction the LORD had commanded Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the instruction of the LORD, which he commanded Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the named appointment and repeat the song’s faithful-love formula.
verses.before: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest who had been chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, “for his steadfast love is forever.”
verses.after: With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest who had been chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, because his faithful love lasts forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest who had been chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, “for his steadfast love is forever.”

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated musicians and their sons’ distinct gate duty.
verses.before: With them, Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for sounding aloud, and instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.
verses.after: Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals to sound, and instruments for the songs of God. Jeduthun’s sons were stationed at the gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: With them, Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for sounding aloud, and instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.

verses.rationale: Preserve the final household blessing and the people’s departure.
verses.before: Then all the people went, each to his home, and David turned to bless his household.
verses.after: Then all the people went home, and David returned to bless his household.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people went, each to his home, and David turned to bless his household.

verses.rationale: Keep the house and tent contrast that begins the house wordplay.
verses.before: After David had settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I am living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under tent curtains.”
verses.after: After David had settled into his house, he said to the prophet Nathan, “Here I am living in a cedar house, while the ark of the LORD’s covenant is under tent curtains.”
verses.tsw_comparator: After David had settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I am living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under tent curtains.”

verses.rationale: Preserve Nathan’s initial response before the later divine correction.
verses.before: Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
verses.after: Nathan told David, “Do whatever is in your heart, for God is with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”

verses.rationale: Keep the temporal turn and the revelation’s recipient.
verses.before: But that night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
verses.after: But that night the word of God came to Nathan:
verses.tsw_comparator: But that night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain the direct prohibition rather than Samuel’s question form.
verses.before: “Go and say to my servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: You are not the one who will build me a house for me to dwell in.
verses.after: “Go and tell my servant David: This is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build me a house to live in.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go and say to my servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: You are not the one who will build me a house for me to dwell in.

verses.rationale: Unfold the elliptical final phrase while preserving the movement among temporary dwellings.
verses.before: For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day, but I have moved from tent to tent and from dwelling place to dwelling place.
verses.after: I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until today. I have moved from tent to tent, from one dwelling place to another.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day, but I have moved from tent to tent and from dwelling place to dwelling place.

verses.rationale: Keep judges and the shepherd image rather than harmonizing Samuel’s tribes.
verses.before: Throughout all the places where I have walked with all Israel, did I ever speak a word to any of Israel’s judges, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’
verses.after: Wherever I traveled with all Israel, did I ever ask any of Israel’s judges, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, ‘Why have you not built me a cedar house?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Throughout all the places where I have walked with all Israel, did I ever speak a word to any of Israel’s judges, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’

verses.rationale: Preserve the pastoral origin and the divine title.
verses.before: “Now then, say this to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be leader over my people Israel.
verses.after: Now tell my servant David: This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now then, say this to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be leader over my people Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep past help leading into the promise of a great name.
verses.before: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make for you a name like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.after: I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make your name like the names of the great ones of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make for you a name like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve planting and the cessation of oppression while continuing the time clause across labels.
verses.before: I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be troubled no more. The children of wickedness will no longer wear them down, as they did at first,
verses.after: I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there. They will live in their own place and be disturbed no more. Violent people will no longer wear them down as they did before,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be troubled no more. The children of wickedness will no longer wear them down, as they did at first,

verses.rationale: Keep the shift from David building a house to receiving a dynastic house.
verses.before: and since the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover, I tell you: the LORD will build you a house.
verses.after: from the time I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. I tell you: the LORD will build you a house.
verses.tsw_comparator: and since the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover, I tell you: the LORD will build you a house.

verses.rationale: Retain death’s ancestral image and the explicit selection from David’s sons.
verses.before: When your days are fulfilled and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one from among your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.after: When your days are complete and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your sons, and establish his kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: When your days are fulfilled and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one from among your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keep house and throne as paired promises.
verses.before: He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
verses.after: He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.

verses.rationale: Preserve the father-son relationship and leave the predecessor unnamed as the source does.
verses.before: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. I will not take my steadfast love away from him, as I took it away from the one who was before you.
verses.after: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. I will not take my faithful love away from him as I took it from the one who was before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. I will not take my steadfast love away from him, as I took it away from the one who was before you.

verses.rationale: Retain my house and my kingdom, a consequential distinction from Samuel.
verses.before: I will establish him in my house and in my kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever.’”
verses.after: I will set him in my house and my kingdom forever, and his throne will stand firm forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will establish him in my house and in my kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever.’”

verses.rationale: Preserve both speech and vision descriptions and complete transmission.
verses.before: Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and according to all this vision.
verses.after: Nathan told David all these words and the whole vision.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and according to all this vision.

verses.rationale: Keep David seated and preserve house as the prayer’s recurring family term.
verses.before: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
verses.after: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. He said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?

verses.rationale: Choose the status reading of the difficult final clause and flag its uncertainty in a note.
verses.before: Yet this was a small thing in your eyes, O God; you have also spoken concerning your servant’s house for a distant future, and you have regarded me according to the order of humankind on high, LORD God.
verses.after: Yet this was a small thing in your eyes, God. You have spoken about your servant’s house far into the future. You have regarded me as a man of high standing, LORD God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet this was a small thing in your eyes, O God; you have also spoken concerning your servant’s house for a distant future, and you have regarded me according to the order of humankind on high, LORD God.

verses.rationale: Retain David’s third-person self-reference and repeated servant language.
verses.before: What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? You know your servant.
verses.after: What more can David say to you about the honor you have given your servant? You know your servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? You know your servant.

verses.rationale: Preserve the servant wording and repeated greatness without substituting the parallel account.
verses.before: O LORD, for the sake of your servant and according to your heart, you have done all this greatness, making known all these great things.
verses.after: LORD, for your servant’s sake and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness and made all these great things known.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, for the sake of your servant and according to your heart, you have done all this greatness, making known all these great things.

verses.rationale: Keep the confession and the explicit hearing image.
verses.before: O LORD, there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.after: LORD, there is no one like you. There is no God besides you, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

verses.rationale: Unfold the long sentence while retaining redemption, the Name, and dispossession.
verses.before: And who is like your people Israel, one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem as a people for himself, to make for yourself a name through great and awe-inspiring deeds, driving out nations before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?
verses.after: And who is like your people Israel, the one nation on earth whose God went out to redeem a people for himself? You made a name for yourself through great and fearsome deeds, driving out nations before your people whom you redeemed from Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And who is like your people Israel, one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem as a people for himself, to make for yourself a name through great and awe-inspiring deeds, driving out nations before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?

verses.rationale: Preserve reciprocal belonging and its permanence.
verses.before: You made your people Israel your people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.
verses.after: You made your people Israel your own people forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You made your people Israel your people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.

verses.rationale: Keep the prayer’s appeal to the spoken promise.
verses.before: “Now, O LORD, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house stand forever, and do as you have spoken.
verses.after: Now, LORD, let the word you have spoken about your servant and his house stand firm forever. Do as you have said.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now, O LORD, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house stand forever, and do as you have spoken.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated Israel titles and the repeated request for stability.
verses.before: Let your name stand and be magnified forever, so that people may say, ‘The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, is God over Israel.’ Let the house of David your servant be established before you.
verses.after: Let it stand firm, and let your name be great forever, so people will say, ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, is God over Israel!’ And let the house of David your servant stand firm before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your name stand and be magnified forever, so that people may say, ‘The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, is God over Israel.’ Let the house of David your servant be established before you.

verses.rationale: Render uncovering the ear as revelation and supply courage for the elliptical found expression.
verses.before: For you, my God, have disclosed to your servant that you will build him a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you.
verses.after: For you, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build him a house. That is why your servant has found the courage to pray before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, my God, have disclosed to your servant that you will build him a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the confession linked to the favorable promise.
verses.before: Now, O LORD, you are God, and you have spoken this good thing concerning your servant.
verses.after: Now, LORD, you are God, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now, O LORD, you are God, and you have spoken this good thing concerning your servant.

verses.rationale: Retain blessing as already given and its repeated permanence.
verses.before: And now, may it please you to bless your servant’s house, that it may continue forever before you. For you, O LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever.”
verses.after: You have been pleased to bless your servant’s house, so that it may remain before you forever. For you, LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, may it please you to bless your servant’s house, that it may continue forever before you. For you, O LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever.”

verses.rationale: Render daughter towns as surrounding towns while retaining Gath.
verses.before: After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them. He took Gath and its surrounding towns from the hand of the Philistines.
verses.after: After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them. He took Gath and its surrounding towns from their control.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them. He took Gath and its surrounding towns from the hand of the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keep political subjection and continuing tribute distinct.
verses.before: He struck Moab, and the Moabites became David’s servants, bringing tribute.
verses.after: He also defeated Moab. The Moabites became David’s subjects and brought him tribute.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck Moab, and the Moabites became David’s servants, bringing tribute.

verses.rationale: Choose Hadadezer as the movement’s subject and clarify the hand idiom as control.
verses.before: David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah toward Hamath, as he went to establish his power at the Euphrates River.
verses.after: David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah toward Hamath, as Hadadezer went to establish his control at the Euphrates River.
verses.tsw_comparator: David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah toward Hamath, as he went to establish his power at the Euphrates River.

verses.rationale: Preserve Chronicles’ exact counts and the injury to the horses.
verses.before: David captured from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left from them one hundred chariot horses.
verses.after: David captured a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers from him. David hamstrung all the chariot horses except enough for a hundred chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: David captured from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left from them one hundred chariot horses.

verses.rationale: Retain the assisting force and casualty count.
verses.before: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans.
verses.after: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans.

verses.rationale: Supply forces for the verb’s missing object and preserve the victory refrain.
verses.before: Then David placed garrisons among the Arameans of Damascus, and the Arameans became David’s servants, bringing tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
verses.after: David stationed forces in Aramean Damascus. The Arameans became his subjects and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David placed garrisons among the Arameans of Damascus, and the Arameans became David’s servants, bringing tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

verses.rationale: Retain the gold objects and their destination.
verses.before: David took the gold shields that had belonged to Hadadezer’s servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.after: David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer’s servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: David took the gold shields that had belonged to Hadadezer’s servants and brought them to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep Chronicles’ place-names and the forward link to temple furnishings.
verses.before: From Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a very great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
verses.after: From Tibhath and Cun, towns belonging to Hadadezer, David took a vast quantity of bronze. Solomon used it to make the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze utensils.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a very great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.

verses.rationale: Retain Tou’s name and continue the response into the next verse.
verses.before: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
verses.after: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah’s entire army,
verses.tsw_comparator: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

verses.rationale: Unfold the parenthetical explanation and preserve all three metals.
verses.before: he sent his son Hadoram to King David, to ask after his welfare and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Hadoram brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze.
verses.after: he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him for fighting Hadadezer and defeating him. Hadadezer had often been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: he sent his son Hadoram to King David, to ask after his welfare and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Hadoram brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze.

verses.rationale: Retain Edom here and all five peoples in the dedication list.
verses.before: King David also dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold that he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
verses.after: King David dedicated these to the LORD as well, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
verses.tsw_comparator: King David also dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold that he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.

verses.rationale: Keep the victory credited to Abishai and the exact total.
verses.before: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck Edom in the Valley of Salt—eighteen thousand.
verses.after: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck Edom in the Valley of Salt—eighteen thousand.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated victory refrain and the immediate unnamed subject.
verses.before: He placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David’s servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
verses.after: He stationed garrisons in Edom, and all Edom became David’s subjects. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David’s servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

verses.rationale: Keep both justice terms and the repeated all-inclusive scope.
verses.before: So David reigned over all Israel, administering justice and righteousness for all his people.
verses.after: David reigned over all Israel, administering justice and righteousness for all his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David reigned over all Israel, administering justice and righteousness for all his people.

verses.rationale: Distinguish military command from the recording office.
verses.before: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
verses.after: Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

verses.rationale: Retain Abimelech and Shavsha rather than harmonizing parallel names.
verses.before: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;
verses.after: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Shavsha was the scribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;

verses.rationale: Keep the two guard groups and Chronicles’ description of the sons’ positions.
verses.before: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites. David’s sons were foremost at the king’s side.
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites. David’s sons held the leading positions at the king’s side.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites. David’s sons were foremost at the king’s side.

verses.rationale: Preserve the succession before the son is named.
verses.before: After this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.
verses.after: After this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated reciprocal kindness and comforting purpose.
verses.before: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the Ammonites, to Hanun, to comfort him.
verses.after: David said, “I will show faithful kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed faithful kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him over his father’s death. David’s servants came to Hanun in Ammonite territory to comfort him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the Ammonites, to Hanun, to comfort him.

verses.rationale: Keep all three hostile allegations within the officials’ speech.
verses.before: But the officials of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Do you think David is honoring your father in your eyes because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you in order to search out, overthrow, and spy out the land?”
verses.after: But the Ammonite officials said to Hanun, “Do you think David is honoring your father by sending comforters? Haven’t his servants come to explore, overthrow, and spy out the land?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the officials of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Do you think David is honoring your father in your eyes because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you in order to search out, overthrow, and spy out the land?”

verses.rationale: Preserve the public bodily humiliation without importing Samuel’s half-beard detail.
verses.before: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, cut off their garments at the middle, at their buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.after: Hanun seized David’s servants, shaved them, cut their clothes in half at the buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, cut off their garments at the middle, at their buttocks, and sent them away.

verses.rationale: Keep David’s practical response and the reason for delaying their return.
verses.before: They went and told David about the men, and he sent messengers to meet them, for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”
verses.after: When David was told about the men, he sent people to meet them, because they were deeply humiliated. The king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, and then return.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They went and told David about the men, and he sent messengers to meet them, for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the stench image, ancient weight, and all three recruiting regions.
verses.before: When the Ammonites saw that they had become hateful to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, from Aram-maacah, and from Zobah.
verses.after: The Ammonites realized they had become a stench to David. Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Ammonites saw that they had become hateful to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, from Aram-maacah, and from Zobah.

verses.rationale: Retain the large chariot figure and the separate Ammonite mobilization.
verses.before: They hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his people. They came and camped before Medeba. And the Ammonites gathered from their cities and came for battle.
verses.after: They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah and his troops. These forces came and camped opposite Medeba. The Ammonites gathered from their towns and came out to battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: They hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his people. They came and camped before Medeba. And the Ammonites gathered from their cities and came for battle.

verses.rationale: Keep Joab’s command and the whole fighting force.
verses.before: When David heard, he sent Joab and the whole army of warriors.
verses.after: When David heard, he sent Joab and the entire army of warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: When David heard, he sent Joab and the whole army of warriors.

verses.rationale: Make the two positions clear for the ensuing divided battle.
verses.before: The Ammonites came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.
verses.after: The Ammonites came out and formed their battle line at the city entrance. The kings who had come were separately positioned in the open country.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Ammonites came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.

verses.rationale: Preserve the two-front threat and the selection of troops.
verses.before: When Joab saw that the battle line was against him in front and behind, he chose some of the best men in Israel and drew them up against Aram.
verses.after: Joab saw that battle threatened him both in front and behind. He chose some of Israel’s best troops and drew them up against the Arameans.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joab saw that the battle line was against him in front and behind, he chose some of the best men in Israel and drew them up against Aram.

verses.rationale: Keep the brother relationship and opposing force assignments.
verses.before: He placed the rest of the people under the command of his brother Abishai, and they drew up against the Ammonites.
verses.after: He put the rest of the troops under his brother Abishai, and they drew up against the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed the rest of the people under the command of his brother Abishai, and they drew up against the Ammonites.

verses.rationale: Retain the reciprocal rescue arrangement.
verses.before: He said, “If Aram is too strong for me, you will be a help to me; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will save you.
verses.after: Joab said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, you must come to my rescue. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will rescue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “If Aram is too strong for me, you will be a help to me; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will save you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated strength language and the open outcome entrusted to the LORD.
verses.before: Be strong, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do what is good in his eyes.”
verses.after: Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in his eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Be strong, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do what is good in his eyes.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the fleeing force without changing the sequence.
verses.before: Then Joab and the people who were with him advanced to battle against Aram, and they fled before him.
verses.after: Joab and the troops with him advanced against the Arameans for battle, and the Arameans fled before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joab and the people who were with him advanced to battle against Aram, and they fled before him.

verses.rationale: Keep the linked retreats and Joab’s return.
verses.before: When the Ammonites saw that Aram had fled, they too fled before his brother Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.
verses.after: When the Ammonites saw the Arameans fleeing, they too fled before Joab’s brother Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Ammonites saw that Aram had fled, they too fled before his brother Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Identify the River geographically and retain Shophach’s form of the name.
verses.before: When Aram saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, with Shophach, commander of Hadadezer’s army, at their head.
verses.after: The Arameans saw that Israel had defeated them. They sent messengers and brought out the Arameans beyond the Euphrates River, led by Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer’s army.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Aram saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, with Shophach, commander of Hadadezer’s army, at their head.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated battle preparations rather than smoothing away the narrative repetition.
verses.before: When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came against them, and drew up against them. David drew up for battle against Aram, and they fought with him.
verses.after: David was told, so he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came against them. He formed his battle line against them. When David drew up against the Arameans, they fought him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came against them, and drew up against them. David drew up for battle against Aram, and they fought with him.

verses.rationale: Retain Chronicles’ counts and infantry category, supplying fighters for chariots as casualties.
verses.before: Aram fled before Israel, and David killed from Aram seven thousand chariot troops and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also put Shophach, commander of the army, to death.
verses.after: The Arameans fled before Israel. David killed seven thousand Aramean chariot fighters and forty thousand foot soldiers, and he killed Shophach, the army commander.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aram fled before Israel, and David killed from Aram seven thousand chariot troops and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also put Shophach, commander of the army, to death.

verses.rationale: Keep submission and the end of further assistance.
verses.before: When Hadadezer’s servants saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with David and served him. And Aram was unwilling to save the Ammonites any longer.
verses.after: When Hadadezer’s subjects saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and served him. The Arameans were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Hadadezer’s servants saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with David and served him. And Aram was unwilling to save the Ammonites any longer.

verses.rationale: Preserve the devastation and David’s location without importing the omitted Bathsheba account.
verses.before: At the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army's forces. He devastated the land of the Ammonites, then came and besieged Rabbah, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and tore it down.
verses.after: At the turn of the year, when kings go out to war, Joab led out the army. He devastated Ammonite territory and came to besiege Rabbah, while David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and demolished it.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army's forces. He devastated the land of the Ammonites, then came and besieged Rabbah, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and tore it down.

verses.rationale: Choose their king for malkam while noting the divine-name alternative and preserving the weight.

verses.after: David took the crown from their king’s head. It weighed a talent of gold and contained a precious stone, and it was placed on David’s head. He carried off a great deal of plunder from the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: David took the crown of their king from his head and found that it weighed a talent of gold, with a precious stone in it. It was placed on David’s head. He also brought out a very great amount of plunder from the city.

verses.rationale: Retain the violent reading of the difficult Hebrew verb and flag the forced-labor alternative without concealing the harm.
